entries.core_move: Verify causality of an LTI system by checking that its impulse response satisfies $h(t)=0 for all t<0 in the pole-based stability setting$.
Classify a causal LTI system as BIBO stable or unstable by checking whether every transfer-function pole lies strictly in the left half of the s-plane.
Recognize left-half-plane poles by using their negative real parts to identify decaying response modes that support BIBO stability in causal LTI systems.
Identify right-half-plane poles by using their positive real parts to infer growing exponential modes and BIBO instability in causal LTI systems.
Classify imaginary-axis poles by recognizing their nondecaying response modes and marking causal LTI systems with such poles as not BIBO stable.
Interpret negative real pole locations as decaying exponential response terms and connect their decay rates to stable causal LTI system behavior.
Identify positive real pole contributions as growing exponential response terms and use their unbounded time-domain growth to classify a causal LTI system as BIBO unstable.
Convert left-half-plane complex-conjugate pole locations into exponentially decaying sinusoidal response terms and their BIBO-stable causal LTI interpretation.
